newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to liberalise fuel supply to cooperatives.
newsitem.headline: Spain to liberalise fuel supply to cooperatives.

text.p: The Spanish cabinet presented a decree introducing deregulatory measures for fuel distribution, Industry Minister Josep Pique said on Friday.
This includes measures allowing direct distribution from suppliers, aimed at increasing competition and cutting prices for consumers in cooperatives.

Striking truckers have been requesting measures to curb surging fuel costs. But as many of them operate independently they have to buy fuel at current petrol station prices, along with small customers.

Direct supply has so far only been allowed for farming cooperatives. "These measures aim to increase competition in the distribution process and are expected, logically, to have a positive impact on prices," the Minister told a press conference after the weekly cabinet meeting.
Pique said that the measure would impact transporters of goods and passengers, as well as marine transporters.
He added that the measure could save these cooperatives five to 10 pesetas per litre.
